verdict.rationale: Proton Pass's own docs describe using stored passkeys to sign into websites: it prompts you to use a passkey on your next visit and lets you choose among multiple passkeys for the same site. That covers the website half of the story beyond TOTP. A 2023 community comment that launch materials did not mention passkeys only reflects timing and does not concretely contradict the current docs. missing for 10: evidence of passkey sign-in to native apps (not just websites), explicit documentation of passkey storage and creation flows across platforms, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an everyday user, the app stores passkeys and signs me into websites and apps with them, not just TOTP codes

citations.quote: Passkeys allow you to authenticate yourself for online accounts without using passwords or passphrases.
Next time you access the site, Proton Pass will prompt you to enter using your passkey.
Note that you can have multiple passkeys for the same site; they will all be displayed in the same pop-up, and you can choose which to use.
